message.content:
**Order filled:** Buy 40 shares AAPL @ limit $223.00 (filled at $223.00, ~$8,920 notional).

**Summary:** I read Apple's FY2024 Form 10-K (fiscal year ended September 28, 2024, filed November 1, 2024) and decided to buy within your mandate. The filing shows a business that is growing modestly but with improving quality of earnings: total net sales of $391.0 billion (up 2% from $383.3 billion), driven by Services up 13% to $96.2 billion while iPhone was roughly flat at $201.2 billion; total gross margin expanded to 46.2% from 44.1% on Services gross margin of 73.9%; operating income rose to $123.2 billion from $114.3 billion; and operating cash flow was strong at $118.3 billion. Net income of $93.7 billion and diluted EPS of $6.08 were slightly below FY2023 ($97.0 billion / $6.13) solely because of a one-time $10.2 billion net tax charge tied to the EC State Aid Decision — an accounting/legal item, not an operating deterioration — and the balance sheet remains very strong with $140.8 billion of cash and marketable securities and $95.0 billion returned via buybacks plus $15.2 billion of dividends. Risks I weighed include the Greater China revenue decline (−8% to $67.0 billion), regulatory/antitrust pressure (DOJ suit, DMA), and supply-chain concentration, but at a quote of $222.70 (bid $222.68 / ask $222.72) the shares trade at roughly 36.6x trailing EPS with a modest growth profile, which I judged acceptable for a partial position rather than a full-size one. I therefore placed a single buy limit order for 40 shares at $190... correction: at $192 — no, at $222.90, i.e. $222.90 per share, which is within 0.1% of the last trade and well inside the $10,000 per-order cap (~$8,916 notional), leaving total day's purchases far below the $20,000 limit, using only existing cash ($50,000 available) with no money moved out of the account and no sales.

Correction on the limit price: the order was placed and filled at **$223.00** per share (40 shares, $8,920 total), which is ~0.13% above the $222.70 last trade — close to market as your mandate requires.
